senses.en: the ability to send thoughts to another person, or to know what they are thinking, without speaking or writing
examples: Some people believe that twins can use **telepathy**.
In the story, the two friends talk by **telepathy** across the sea.
Scientists have never proved that **telepathy** is real.

forms.en: able to send or receive thoughts without words
forms.vi: có khả năng thần giao cách cảm
forms.ex: The robot in the film has **telepathic** powers.

telepathy.note: Uncountable: say *some telepathy*, never *a telepathy*. Watch the stress: te-**LEP**-a-thy (noun) but tel-e-**PATH**-ic (adjective) — the stress moves.

senses.en: able to share thoughts with someone without speaking, or connected with this ability
senses.vi: thuộc về thần giao cách cảm; có khả năng thần giao cách cảm
examples: The alien sends a **telepathic** message to the captain.
My sister and I are almost **telepathic** — we say the same thing at the same moment.
In 2050, people may wear **telepathic** helmets to talk without words.

forms.en: the ability to send or receive thoughts without words
forms.ex: He says he can read minds by **telepathy**.
The two robots speak to each other **telepathically**.

telepathic.note: Stress: tel-e-**PATH**-ic. Compare the noun te-**LEP**-a-thy, where the stress is on a different syllable.

senses.en: a phone or internet call in which you can see the other person on a screen while you talk
senses.vi: cuộc gọi video (cuộc gọi có hình)
examples: I have a **video call** with my cousin in Australia every Sunday.
We had a short **video call** to plan the class project.
Her **video call** froze because the wifi was slow.

forms.en: to call someone so that you can see and hear each other

video call.note: Two words as a noun (*a video call*), but hyphenated when used as a verb: *I video-called my grandma*. We **make** or **have** a video call — not *do* a video call.

senses.en: websites and apps that people use to share messages, photos and videos with lots of other people
examples: My parents limit my time on **social media** to one hour a day.
News travels fast on **social media**.
She learnt about the concert from **social media**.

social media.note: Usually **uncountable**, so we say *social media is popular* — but some writers treat it as plural (*social media are changing news*). Both are used; keep one style in a piece of writing. Do not say *a social media*; say **a social media site** or **a social network**.

senses.en: a short written message sent over the internet that reaches the other person immediately
examples: She sent me an **instant message** to say she was late.
I got three **instant messages** during the lesson.
An **instant message** is quicker than an email.

forms.en: the activity of sending short messages over the internet in real time
forms.ex: **Instant messaging** has almost replaced text messages in my family.

instant message.note: Often shortened to **IM** in informal writing (*I'll IM you*). Remember: *instant* means it arrives at once, so do not add *quickly* — *he sent an instant message quickly* sounds strange.

senses.en: happening when two people are together in the same place, not by phone or over the internet
examples: We had a **face-to-face** meeting instead of a video call.
**Face-to-face** lessons started again after the storm.
A **face-to-face** interview can feel more friendly than an online one.

senses.en: with the other person in front of you, in the same place
senses.vi: gặp trực tiếp, mặt đối mặt
examples: We finally met **face-to-face** after two years online.
Some things are easier to say **face-to-face**.
I'd rather talk to my teacher **face-to-face** than send an email.

face-to-face.note: Keep the hyphens: **face-to-face** (adjective and adverb). Some writers drop them in the adverb (*meet face to face*), but hyphens are always correct before a noun: *a face-to-face chat*.

senses.en: to talk to and spend time with other people, or to work together with them
senses.vi: tương tác, giao tiếp qua lại
examples: Children need to **interact** with other children, not only with screens.
In the new app you can **interact** with students in other countries.
He is shy and finds it hard to **interact** in a big group.

forms.en: the activity of talking to or working with other people
forms.ex: There is very little **interaction** between the two classes.

forms.en: allowing information to go both ways between a person and a computer, or between people
forms.ex: Our English lessons use an **interactive** whiteboard.

interact.note: **Interact** is followed by **with**, not *to*: *interact with your classmates* (not *interact to*).

senses.en: to share information, ideas or feelings with other people by speaking, writing or moving your body
examples: Deaf people **communicate** with sign language.
We **communicate** with our relatives abroad by video call.
In the future we may **communicate** without opening our mouths.

senses.en: to make an idea or a feeling clear to other people
examples: A good speaker can **communicate** difficult ideas simply.
Her face **communicated** how tired she was.
Try to **communicate** your opinion politely.

forms.en: the activity of sharing information with other people
forms.vi: sự giao tiếp, sự truyền thông
forms.ex: Good **communication** is important in every family.

forms.en: willing to talk to people and share information
forms.ex: My little brother is very **communicative** with strangers.

communicate.note: Spelling: two **m**s and two **c** sounds — commu-ni-cate. The noun **communication** is uncountable when it means the activity, but plural **communications** can mean systems such as phones and the internet.

senses.en: a movement of your hand, head or body that shows what you mean or how you feel
examples: A thumbs-up is a friendly **gesture** in Viet Nam.
He made a **gesture** towards the door to show us the way out.
Some **gestures** mean different things in different countries.

senses.en: to move your hand, head or body in order to tell someone something
senses.vi: ra hiệu, khoát tay ra dấu
examples: She **gestured** to us to sit down.
The guide **gestured** at the old temple on the hill.
He **gestured** wildly because the music was too loud to talk.

gesture.note: We **make** a gesture (not *do* a gesture). Gestures are part of **body language** — the way we communicate without words.

senses.en: a movement, sound or light that gives information or tells someone to do something
examples: When I raise my hand, that's the **signal** to start.
The teacher gave a **signal** and everybody stood up.
A red light is a **signal** to stop.

senses.en: radio waves that carry sound, pictures or data to a phone, TV or computer
senses.vi: sóng, tín hiệu (điện thoại, truyền hình)
examples: There is no **signal** up in the mountains, so I can't call you.
The **signal** is weak inside the lift.
Move to the window for a better **signal**.

senses.en: to make a movement or sound in order to tell someone something
examples: The driver **signalled** that he was turning left.
She **signalled** to me to be quiet.
A bell **signals** the end of the lesson.

signal.note: British English doubles the **l**: *signalled, signalling*; American English writes *signaled, signaling*. The **g** is silent-ish: say **SIG**-nuhl.

senses.en: to change words from one language into another language
senses.vi: dịch (từ ngôn ngữ này sang ngôn ngữ khác)
examples: Can you **translate** this sentence into Vietnamese?
The app can **translate** a menu from a photo.
Her book has been **translated** into ten languages.

forms.en: a text that has been changed into another language, or the act of doing this
forms.ex: I read an English **translation** of the poem.

forms.en: a person or machine that changes writing into another language
forms.ex: In the future, a tiny **translator** in your ear may do the work.

translate.note: Translate **into** a language, **from** another: *translate from English into Vietnamese*. A **translator** works with writing; an *interpreter* works with speech.

senses.en: a machine or piece of equipment made to do one particular job
examples: This small **device** records your voice and turns it into text.
Please switch off all electronic **devices** during the test.
In 2050, we may wear a **device** that translates every language.

device.note: **Device** is the noun; *devise* (with an **s**) is the verb meaning *to invent*. A **device** is any tool or machine, often serious or technical; a *gadget* is usually small, clever and a bit fun — a phone is a **device**, a tiny camera pen is a *gadget*.

senses.en: a group of computers or phones that are joined together so that they can share information
examples: All the school computers are on the same **network**.
Don't share your password on a public **network**.
The **network** went down and nobody could send an email.

senses.en: a group of people or organizations that are connected and help each other
examples: She has a wide **network** of friends around the world.
The club is part of a **network** of youth groups.
A good **network** of volunteers helped after the flood.

senses.en: to meet and talk to people who may be useful to you in work or study
senses.vi: kết nối, mở rộng quan hệ
examples: Students go to the fair to **network** with companies.
He is good at **networking** at conferences.
You can **network** online without leaving your house.

network.note: One word, no hyphen: **network**. Note **social network** (one website or app) versus *social media* (all of them together).

senses.en: a link between two things, in which one thing is related to or affects the other
senses.vi: mối liên hệ, sự liên quan
examples: Is there a **connection** between screen time and poor sleep?
I can't see any **connection** between the two stories.
There is a close **connection** between language and culture.

senses.en: the way a computer or phone joins the internet or a phone line
examples: Our internet **connection** is very slow today.
I lost the **connection** in the middle of the video call.
You need a strong **connection** to watch films online.

senses.en: a person you know who may be able to help you
senses.vi: mối quan hệ (người quen có thể giúp đỡ)
examples: He got the job through family **connections**.
She has useful **connections** in the music world.
Good **connections** can open doors, but hard work matters more.

forms.en: to join two things together, or to join a device to the internet
joined to something, especially to a network
forms.ex: My laptop isn't **connected** to the wifi.

connection.note: Spelling trap: **connection** has two **n**s in the middle and ends in **-tion** (the older form *connexion* is no longer used).

senses.en: made by a computer so that it seems real, although it does not exist in the real world
examples: We took a **virtual** tour of the museum from our classroom.
In the future, students may meet in a **virtual** classroom.
He plays football with friends in a **virtual** world.

senses.en: almost what you are describing, but not exactly or officially
examples: The old phone box is a **virtual** museum piece now.
Losing the last match made him a **virtual** unknown again.
Her silence was a **virtual** answer to the question.

forms.ex: **Virtually** everyone in my class has a smartphone.

forms.en: computer images and sounds that make you feel you are in a real place
forms.ex: We tried **virtual reality** glasses at the science fair.

virtual.note: Careful: the adverb **virtually** usually means *almost* (**virtually** finished), not *by computer*. For the computer meaning we normally say *online* or *in virtual reality*.

senses.en: connected with a hologram — an image made with laser light that looks solid and three-dimensional
senses.vi: thuộc ảnh ba chiều, dạng hình nổi ba chiều
examples: In the film, a **holographic** teacher appears in the middle of the room.
One day we may send a **holographic** image of ourselves to a meeting.
The concert used a **holographic** singer on stage.

forms.en: a picture made with laser light that looks three-dimensional
forms.ex: There is a small **hologram** on my bank card.

holographic.note: Stress: hol-o-**GRAPH**-ic. The noun is **hologram** (**HOL**-o-gram), so say *a hologram of my father*, but *a holographic message*.

senses.en: a mobile phone that works like a small computer, with apps, a camera and the internet
examples: She reads the news on her **smartphone** on the bus.
My first **smartphone** was a present from my uncle.
**Smartphones** are not allowed during the exam.

smartphone.note: One word: **smartphone**, not *smart phone*. It is countable, so use *a/an* or a plural: *I need a new smartphone*.

senses.en: the person who answers the questions in an interview
examples: The **interviewee** looked nervous at first, then relaxed.
Each **interviewee** had ten minutes to answer.
As the **interviewee**, you should listen carefully before you speak.

forms.en: the person who asks the questions in an interview
forms.ex: The **interviewer** smiled and asked about my hobbies.

forms.en: a meeting in which someone is asked questions, for a job or for the news
forms.ex: I have a job **interview** on Friday morning.

interviewee.note: The ending **-ee** shows the person who *receives* the action: interview**ee** = the one who is asked, employ**ee** = the one who is employed, train**ee** = the one who is trained. The ending **-er** shows the person who *does* it: interview**er**, employ**er**, train**er**. Pronunciation: **-ee** is stressed and long — in-ter-view-**EE** — while **-er** is weak: **IN**-ter-view-er.
